findings.text: The type assertion changed from `Mock` to `*Mock`. The deprecated call `AssertExpectationsForObjects(t, myMock.Mock)` passes a Mock value, which no longer matches. It falls through to `obj.(assertExpectationser)`, and a Mock value lacks the pointer-receiver methods, so this panics instead of handling it. A `*Mock` argument now logs the deprecation warning spuriously.

raw:
Problems: the type assertion changed from Mock to *Mock. Passing a Mock value (the deprecated path) now falls to obj.(assertExpectationser), which panics because Mock value doesn't implement the pointer-receiver methods. Also, a *Mock passed now logs the deprecation message, and a *Mock does implement assertExpectationser, so that part works but logs a spurious warning. Copying a Mock by value with an embedded mutex is also a concern (go vet).
